name: Vår Energi ASA
reason: North Sea oil & gas producer whose earnings are set by commodity prices: EPS (USD) swung from -0.65 in 2020 to 0.38 in 2022 and 0.29 in 2025, with consensus FY2/FY3 at -32%/-27%; Eni-controlled with low float.

name: Cimpress Plc
reason: Levered web-to-print roll-up with erratic EPS (USD -7.08 in 2023, 6.43 in 2024, 0.58 in 2025), 10y average ROIC of 1.2%, and net debt/EBITDA of 3.76x after debt-funded buybacks (81% of FCF).

name: Pirelli & C. S.p.A.
reason: Mature tyre maker with 10y revenue CAGR of 0.7%, 10y average ROIC of 4.0%, and EPS (EUR) of 0.50 in 2025 still below 0.75 in 2014; consensus FY2/FY3 growth is only 6.8%/8.2% and the Sinochem shareholder dispute adds governance risk.

name: FirstGroup plc
reason: UK bus and rail operator dependent on government contracts, with a 10y average EBIT margin of 1.4% now at a record 3.6% (100th pctile), flat revenue (-0.9%/yr) and consensus LTG of -5.8% in GBP.

name: AMG Critical Materials N.V.
reason: Lithium, vanadium and tantalum producer whose earnings follow commodity prices: EPS (USD) went 5.73 in 2022 to -1.03 in 2024, with negative 10y FCF conversion (-0.65) and net debt/EBITDA of 3.68x.

name: Wavestone SA
reason: Net-cash consulting firm with a 17.6% 10y EPS CAGR (EUR 0.68 to 3.45) but labour-based billing faces the AI threat (as for EPAM/G/EXLS), margin is sliding (11.8% vs a 13.6% average) and consensus LTG is only 2.7%.

name: Bossard Holding AG
reason: Cyclical fastener distributor with a 10y EPS CAGR of 2.8% (CHF 9.44 in 2025 vs a 13.49 peak in 2022), margin at the 9th pctile, and acquisitions absorbing 65% of FCF; no route to >=7% organic growth.

name: Shell Plc
reason: Integrated oil major whose earnings are set by oil, gas and refining prices: adjusted EPS (USD) went 0.62 in 2020 to 5.43 in 2022 to 3.15 in 2025, and the 10y revenue CAGR is -0.3%.

name: freenet AG
reason: German mobile reseller and TV business with a 10y revenue CAGR of -2.4% and EPS CAGR of 3.4% (EUR), margin at a record 14.5% (100th pctile), and a 47.6% gap between adjusted and GAAP earnings: an ordinary business that is cheap.

name: Fugro NV
reason: Offshore geo-survey contractor tied to the energy and wind capex cycle: losses in 2015-20, then EPS (EUR) of 2.29 in 2024 falling to 0.54 in 2025, with shares outstanding up 7.4%/yr over 10 years.

name: Airtel Africa Plc
reason: African telecom and mobile-money franchise with a 33% EBIT margin, but EPS reported in USD swings with naira and CFA devaluations (0.16 in FY21, 0.08 in FY24, 0.19 in FY25); EM regulatory and FX risk make it unforecastable, and Bharti control means low float.

name: AJ Bell Plc
reason: High-quality UK investment platform (38% 10y average ROIC, net cash, EPS GBP 0.07 to 0.26 over FY19-25), but revenue depends on market levels and interest on client cash, and EPS and margin are at 10y highs after the rate tailwind; this matches the wealth-manager and MORN rule.

name: Canal+ SA
reason: Pay-TV group with GAAP losses in 2023-25 (EPS EUR -0.05 in 2025), net debt/EBITDA of 3.67x after the transformational MultiChoice acquisition (acquisitions 1.46x FCF), and only a 5-year public record.

name: OMV Aktiengesellschaft
reason: Austrian oil, gas and chemicals group with commodity-set earnings: adjusted EPS (EUR) went 12.75 in 2022 to 5.94 in 2025, consensus FY2/FY3 is -13%/-19%, and it is controlled by the Austrian state (ÖBAG) and ADNOC.

name: Transocean Ltd.
reason: Offshore driller dependent on the oil capex cycle with adjusted losses in 2017-24, shares outstanding up 10.2%/yr, a 10y average ROIC of -6.3%, and net debt/EBITDA of 3.65x.

name: Hacksaw AB
reason: Exceptional iGaming content supplier (82% EBIT margin, EPS EUR 0.05 to 0.50 over 2022-25, net cash), but a 4-year record of hit-driven games and gambling-regulation risk (revenue from grey markets) make 5-10 years unforecastable.

name: Gestamp Automocion S.A.
reason: Auto body-parts supplier with a ~5% EBIT margin, 10y average ROIC of 4.3%, EPS (EUR) of 0.27 in 2025 vs 0.49 in 2023, and earnings tied to global auto production; cheap but ordinary.

name: Befesa SA
reason: Steel-dust and aluminium recycler whose earnings follow zinc prices and EAF steel volumes: EPS (EUR) went 2.82 in 2021 to 1.38 in 2024, and growth came from the US AZR acquisition (acquisitions 1.01x 10y FCF) at 2.44x net debt/EBITDA.

name: United Internet AG
reason: German telecom and hosting holding company with a 10y EPS CAGR of -1.1% (EUR 1.54 in 2025 vs 2.49 in 2017), margin at the 9th pctile, net debt/EBITDA of 4.19x, and execution risk from the 1&1 network build.

name: Bayer AG
reason: Pharma and crop-science conglomerate with a 10y EPS CAGR of -3.1% (EUR 7.94 in 2022 to 4.91 in 2025), an ongoing glyphosate litigation overhang from the Monsanto deal, and a 313.8% average gap between adjusted and GAAP earnings.
